verdict.tagline: A charmingly dark blend of dungeon crawling and cult management.
for_you_if: you enjoy mixing roguelike combat with colony management
you appreciate dark themes wrapped in cute visuals
you want accessibility options to customize your difficulty
not_for_you_if: you dislike heavy micromanagement and routine chores
you experience controller recognition issues on your hardware
you find base upkeep loops tedious or punishing

claims.claim: Reviewers report controller recognition issues with specific hardware like PS5 and Xbox controllers.

citations.review_text:
Sometimes, there seems to be a consensus from the player base about one game, it's either amazing or terrible. Here, people seems to massively enjoy this game. So, what follows is going to be my impressions and opinion, and that only. If you enjoy the game, and statistically, there's a high chance you do, all the good for you.

Well, you guessed it, I don't like Cult of the Lamb. Wait, let me rephrase that: I really don't like Cult of the Lamb. No, one more time: I HATE Cult of the Lamb.
Like a fool, given the overwhelmingly positive reviews, I bought the game and all the DLCs all at once, thinking I was going to be in for a treat and I might as well get it all since it was on a small sale.

And then I started it... Oh boy!

First of all, it's extremely janky and buggy, it took me a while to make it work as it was not recognizing the controller that it recommends me to play with, despite the fact that literally every single other game I play does (and we're talking about a PS5 controller, not some obscure cheap one bought for 10€).
But once I got this working, my excitement very quickly fell crashing down to the ground.

The visual style looked so unique and appealing on screenshots, but once you're playing it, to me it looks awful. It's very confusing, there's no sense of depth despite it making it look like there is, it really feels like a mobile game. And when I check out the developers, I see that prior, to this game, all they made was mobile and web browser games, and you can tell. If you know where to look, you can also see that it's terribly coded, and it matters because the experience is seriously hindered by it.

So I was already getting less and less excited about it just in the first few minutes. But it kept getting worse. The controls are horrible and don't feel responsive, again feels like a mobile game.
I was expecting to be building a base and managing my cult, as the main tag for the game is BASE BUILDING. But this is clearly not what the game is abo…
Does not work at all with Mac + XBox controller, even after recommending it. Complete waste of two hours of my life trying to figure out how to play this game

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: As the loop settles in, players encounter repetitive base chores and basic combat alongside the core blend.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game combines dungeon exploration with cult management mechanics where players must feed followers, build structures, and clean up waste.

citations.review_text: I don’t get this game. I played it co-op with my partner and we were having fun for the first few hours but that eroded pretty quickly. The dungeons were fine but did start to feel a little bland and repetitive after about 6 hours or so. The real problem was the cult management. It began to feel like a drag on the game as it took a lot of micromanagement for simple tasks and it lacked quality of life features to make managing the followers easier. We spent so much time running around the base doing menial tasks like cleaning up poo, making food, repairing beds, running a sermon everyday, etc, that it felt like a chore stopping us from making meaningful decisions and actually playing the game. Some people say this gets better late game as you unlock the tech to automate the base properly but my question is why not give us this from the start? What is gained by making the early game so boring I couldn’t be bothered to get through it? It’s a shame I feel this way about the game because I think the idea is good and I love the art and music but the game play just falls flat.

Cult Management on a Chill: Balancing Faith, Cauliflower, and Crusades
Cult of the Lamb delivers a surprisingly therapeutic loop wrapped in a dark, occult aesthetic. The core of the game is all about a delicate balance of faith, routine, and bloody crusades. It’s incredibly satisfying to just chill, run through the biomes, slash down heretics, collect bones, defeat bosses, and gather curses. The combat feels snappy, and the overall pacing allows you to enjoy the action without unnecessary stress.
However, the real charm (and the real micro-management) begins when you return to your camp. To keep your cult from collapsing and your followers from defecting, you have to constantly improve their general well-being, build structures, and fulfill their randomized, sometimes absurd requests. The gameplay turns into a weirdly cozy domestic routine: you are harvesting Camellia flowers to heal your sick minions, cooking proper meals out of cauliflower, and literally cleaning the map from follower poop and vomit. If you look past the grim facade, it’s a beautifully designed, meditative corner where you hold absolute authority over a flock that completely relies on your guidance.
I highly recommend this to anyone who wants to build a stylish, twisted home and enjoys the rhythm of gentle management mixed with satisfying heretic-slashing.

Cult of the Lamb is a brilliant blend of two distinct gameplay genres that complement each other seamlessly. The action packed combat with its varied weapons and spells balances perfectly with returning to your base to manage resources and care for your followers.
Beyond the gameplay loop, the art style and overall vibe are incredible. Even though the game recommends playing with a controller, I use a mouse and keyboard and haven't found it clunky or frustratingly hard at all. Absolutely love this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the combat system feels basic or repetitive over extended play sessions.

citations.review_text: Maybe it's just not my preference but it gets kind of boring. Even as you continue to explore, the enemies' attack patterns are more or less the same, and I never got really attached to any of the followers so it felt grindy and really repetitive. The artstyle is the biggest redeeming quality, and the music is nice too.

It's... good. And that's the problem. Sort of. It's not amazing, but it's good enough that you keep playing. The combat feels smooth, but it's also super basic. Thankfully, the runs are short, because that combat probably wouldn't hold up for much longer. The town-building gives you just enough to keep you busy, but it's basic too.

Your cultists are cute but are basically fuel for your own progression. They dont really have a personality and they age and die surprisingly quickly. Sure, you can get married, you can even have a polyamorous marraige, but I didn't feel a thing when I sacrificed my spouses for my rituals. Then again, maybe that's the point.

It's baby's first roguelite, and a damn good one at that. It's simple, accessible, and knows how to keep you entertained. But once you look past how well it executes its ideas, there's not much depth to any of them. It's a great entry point into the genre, but it also feels like it never quite grows beyond that.

6.5/10

Very cute relaxing game
it strikes a fun balance between an action packed rougelike action and taking care of your cult
dlc is also well worth the price and adds plenty of more stuff to do.
An all around enjoyable experience and and easy favorite of mine.
Amazing game!  A mix of harvest moon and binding of issac. My crop will be sacrificed for my eternal glory!

Very cute and very gory
Good combo of rougelike and tycoon sim
Art style is amazing and the combat is simple but flows nice

Cult of the Lamb takes the best of other games adjacent to it and puts a cute, yet demonic, twist on it. There are elements in the game akin to stardew valley, such as the fishing and farming mechanics, an ability to marry a follower and others together (Woolhaven). The cult management is similar to Rimworld without the strict priority schedule. I have found great enjoyment in building and managing my cult as well as crusading. Although things can get repetitive, Woolhaven DLC solves this by putting more urgency on taking care of your cult and a need to go out to crusade during bad winters. I have become so attatched to some followers i do anything in my power to resurrect them or make them young again. This is a solid 9/10 game for me and i highly recommend this game to others who are into colony sims and dungeon crawlers. 

Bonus points for the cuteness !
YES omg this game is like if you combine a rougelike with a base management game, and it works so well together!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that many bosses spawn additional fodder enemies during fights, which some find annoying.

citations.review_text:
A true, triumphant feat in duality. 
It nails the balance between the combat and base-building aspects.

The progression is smooth sailing all through and through. 
You have to tend to your cult, and your cult will reward you handsomely for that.
You have to go out for crusades, and the rewards will ensure that you are able to expand your cult easily.
Figuring out how to balance between these two things was really, really enjoyable. 
The key is to keep an eye of the number of your followers so you will be able to identify the rate of food consumption, amount of Camelia you have so that you will be prepared for a possible cult pandemic. 
I love things like that, and I love it even more by the fact that it does not get annoying.
Be smart about the logistics and pays off!

Combat is nice and simple, like really, the weapons are fun to play with- especially my beloved Blunderbuss. The gauntlet sucked. Not my style. But I know there is something for everyone.
Other than that, I noticed that a lot of these bosses have fodder spawns. I dislike that design trope in boss fights honestly, but it is manageable.

Learn how to dodge and you are set. The invincibility frames provided by your dodge are quite generous, all things considered. If you suck at it, you may tweak the accessibility settings to your liking. That helped me to get the base game 100% faster because some parts were too grindy (looking at you, follower forms).

There is so much to do and to be offered in this game. 
I was constantly wowed by the fact that I was unlocking new mechanics when I was already done with 3/5 of the Bishops. It becomes a fact more impressive since you will not be overwhelmed by what you are being thrown at.

The story was integrated well into the game. Has such a satisfying payoff. What's there not to love?
It is even accompanied with an artstyle that has so much soul. It is so, so cute.

Go and play it. 
I was so intrigued that I was completely willing to pay the full price for it.
[b]…

I love this game and its so addicting. The only two things keeping me from giving it a 10/10 is that the game keeps alot of necessary information from you. It doesn't tell you that if you make a follower too sinful, they get yoinked from your cult and it doesn't tell you that the power to "freeze time", aka freeze enemies in place, doesn't actually do that, because if enemies are in the middle of attacking, they will still finish their attack while time is frozen. 

Another thing is just enemy design, which is just a pesonal preference. I dislike when bosses spawn in a bunch of other enemies, because it's just annoying, imo. Just make it more bullet hell, or make the boss attack faster, or have more complicated attacks that you have to learn and predict, make the actual boss harder. I want to fight the actual boss, not draw out the fight by hitting fodder that just absorb damage while posing barely any threat to me. I think the bosses could have more creativity, rather than just "throw five million meat shields at the player, that'll make it harder". 

Another personal preference: dagger and gauntlets are trash, just sayin.

TLDR: 9/10, please give more info to the player and make harder bossfights that dont spawn bunch of fodder, and its 10/10 for sure. Though I havent played Woolhaven yet, and people say the bosses there are way better, so like yeah :3

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the base management aspect as becoming tedious and punishing when leaving the cult alone for too long to go on crusades.

citations.review_text:
I'll start with the bad so I can at least end on the positives (because there are positives I'm just gonna rant for a bit):
Cult of the Lamb was... fine. I enjoyed playing it, but this game felt very ocean-wide, puddle-deep. It's trying to be a colony manager and roguelike at the same time and only executing each of those at maybe 50%. The colony management gets really tedious after a while and there's certain things you just can't automate. So if I decide to breed cultists to make some new ones, if I want to have that cultist start with good levels, I have to then spend several full days (I think close to a week) in-game just kissing an egg and petting a baby. Mind you, I've already automated most of my cult so there's really not a ton I can do.

The challenge, however, is that while you may say "just kiss the egg and go on a roguelike run for that day" - that doesn't really work out how you'd like to to. Yes you can do a really rushed run where you skip rooms, but you can't extend a run at all to loop it nor can you take your time with it. Because if you do either of those the timer is going to pass another day and you've missed the nurturing chance. If I can automate pretty much everything, why tf can't I tell my cultists WHO MADE THE CHILD to take care of that child?

This made is so that I just had to sit around in my base doing various small nothing-tasks trying to waste time until that baby developed into a full adult cultist, maybe occasionally rushing to do a roguelike run if I felt like I could squeeze one in. But combined with certain other tasks requiring my intervention, I just felt very tied down to the cult most of the time. 

And then the roguelike sections are just... not rewarding. It felt like this game took the concept of roguelike and decided to remove the fun parts. Where are the broken item combos? Or just item combos in general. The biggest influence on a run's success felt like if I lucked into a strong starting weapon or not. Past that the …

It's a good game, but I kind of got to the point where the base management felt a little tedious. I spent quite a bit of time working on my base and trying to keep my Cult members happy and fed. I ended up almost maxing out everything in my Cult before I even beat the second boss. In a sense, I started to feel openly punished for even leaving at any point to do Crusades (what the game calls the combat portion of the game). If I left my Cult alone for too long, there would start to be rebellions and people dying or babies weren't being cared for, etc. There was a point I had to just stop caring what happened to my Cult members and go Crusade just to finish the game.

I think it said it took me about a day and 15 hours to complete the base level game, with no postgame. I lost interest when I encountered a bug after initiating Woolhaven that my main Shrine would not work as intended. There was a back-up save before Woolhaven which would have sent me back only a few hours prior. However, I realized I was starting to feel like taking care of my Cult was almost like a second job. As a Dad with limited gaming time, I want to spend as much time in the parts of a game I like these days and less time in things I find tedious. It's probably not too much of an issue if you enjoy management games like that and have the time to thoroughly enjoy it.

As for the Crusades themselves; they are overall fun and resemble bullet-hell types of games. There isn't too much difficulty to them, which I liked. One part though is that you have to go with what it randomly decides you are going to use at the start of the Crusade. You later get to influence this using your money. Some weapons are really good and other ones kind of suck, in my opinion. The Axe and Blunderbuss are really good weapons, but the Gauntlets kind of suck and I generally have to leave the Crusade early if I'm about to fight a harder boss using them. I liked using the Sword, but I rarely saw it after I left the Darkwoods ar…

Honestly I cant recommend this game enough. I disagree with people who say that because the game divides attention between hack'n slash and base building aspects both parts of the game feels half baked. 
The base building & management part of the game is very good (though at times overly punishing) and is very relaxing once you have a good setup and aren't struggling for resources, though without good setup it can be quite difficult, as your followers will quickly eat through much of the resources you are able to gather. This being said, I thoroughly enjoyed managing my own little cult, and I think most (if not all) of the mechanics are well implemented, and especially in the mid-late game it provides lots of ways to impact the dungeon crawl sections. 
The crusades (dungeon crawl segments) are also really fun, and while the combat isn't as complex or intense as say, Hades; the vast variety of weapons, spells (and in the DLC, legendary weapons) more than makes up for this. The combat feels clean and crisp and the enemies are well designed and distinctive. The bosses and minibosses feel well thought out and give challenge without feeling too confusing or unfair. (the game also offers many difficulty settings as well as various assist options if its too hard) Personally I play on hard difficulty and would probably recommend hard or above to anyone familiar with dungeon crawlers. The tarot card & fleece systems provide fun ways to customise builds each run and honestly it manages to not get too repetitive. The combat is overall fast-paced and I haven't really had any moments when I felt a boss was too tanky or otherwise badly designed. The soundtrack is good, though nothing crazy exceptional. The one thing I would say is that if you come into the game expecting the base building to be optional and expect to just play a hades-esque game you will probably be disappointed especially if you dont like base-builders.
